Their research focus spans several educational and technological domains, including student assessment and achievement, online and distance learning, science education, information systems, youth and family, mathematics education, and instructional design. Based on the available data, they have supervised work involving structural equation modeling, mobile application screening tools, and flipped classroom models.

In 2023, they advised a study titled "Determinants of Student Learning Satisfaction and Academic Performance in High School Chemistry: a Prediction Model Building Study for Online Learning." This research focused on online and distance learning, student assessment and achievement, and science education. The work specifically investigated factors influencing student learning satisfaction and academic performance among high school chemistry students at the Philippine Science High School Cordillera Administrative Region Campus.

In 2022, they advised a thesis titled "Assessing Dyscalculic Tendencies Among Children Through a Mobile Application Screening Tool." The sub-topics for this work include information systems and youth and family. The research involved the use of a mobile application as a screening tool for dyscalculic tendencies.

In 2020, they advised a thesis titled "Team-based Flipped Classroom: Effects on Student Attitude, Motivation, Engagement, and Achievement in Mathematics." This project addressed sub-topics of mathematics education, student assessment and achievement, and instructional design. The study utilized a mixed-methods approach to investigate how the team-based flipped classroom model affects student attitude, motivation, engagement, and achievement in mathematics compared to a conventional classroom setting.

While Maria Ana T. Quimbo has three advised theses listed in this repository, they have no articles of their own currently recorded in this repository. Their most recent advised thesis was in 2023, and they have no advisees listed for 2026. Their supervision patterns show a focus on how instructional models and digital tools impact student outcomes across different subjects and age groups. They have demonstrated experience in supervising research that combines educational theory with technological applications, such as mobile tools and online learning environments. The breadth of their supervision covers various educational levels, from grade 3 pupils to high school students.
